title: Elastic Phase Harmonizer — adaptive phase splitting to balance latency and throughput
creator: Ava Morales
description:
Problem: Prefill/decode scheduling currently uses rigid phase split heuristics that either favor throughput (larger consolidated prefill batches) or latency (aggressive phase isolation). Current approaches show tenant starvation during microbursts and suboptimal GPU kernel utilization when attention sparsity varies across requests.

Goal: Implement an "Elastic Phase Harmonizer" — a scheduler component that adaptively smooths phase boundaries and issues kernel hints based on short-term workload signals (sequence length distribution, attention sparsity estimate, request deadline/priority). Harmonizer should trade off per-tenant fairness, tail latency, and aggregate throughput according to configurable policies.

Scope: design + simulator + runtime prototype + experiment-run + rollout. Focus areas: dynamic phase window sizing, kernel hint propagation to kernel-selection layer, per-tenant fairness score, hedging thresholds, and safe canary rollout with rollback triggers.
acceptance_criteria: P99 end-to-end latency for latency-priority tenant improves by >=10% in microburst workloads compared to baseline stable-split policy
Aggregate throughput reduction <= 5% under steady-state mixed workloads
Fairness index (Jain) across tenants increases from baseline by >=0.08 in burst scenarios
No increase in GPU OOM incidents or KV-cache eviction rate in 72-hour soak
Automated rollback if error rate or tail latency regresses beyond SLA (slo-monitor alert)
Design doc and runtime tests merged; monitoring dashboards created and linked
work_log: 2026-02-11: Kickoff sync with runtime and kernels teams. Agreed on signals: seq_len_hist (last 30s), prefill_queue_depth, attn_sparsity_hint (binary), tenant_priority_tag.

2026-02-13: Simulator (qsim variant) integrated with synthetic workloads: short-chatty, long-context, mixed-sparsity. Initial sweep showed 12% P99 reduction for latency-priority tenant at moderate load.
2026-02-15: Prototype harmonizer API defined: compute_window(requests) -> phase_plan {split_points, kernel_hint, hedge_score}. Exposed as gRPC call from arbiter to kernel-probe router.
2026-02-18: Microbenchmark on p4d cluster: kernel hinting reduced small-attn kernel launch overhead by ~9% when batching aligned to suggested splits.

2026-02-20: Integration test failure observed: eviction spikes when harmonizer merges long prefill slices; introduced conservative cache-preservation rule (limit merged-prefill span during high-KV-use by tenant).
decisions: Prefer adaptive smoothing over fixed thresholds: use exponentially-weighted moving average on seq_len_hist with anomaly detection for microburst detection.
Propagate kernel_hint as a soft suggestion (weight 0.6) to kernel-selection to allow fallbacks when hardware constraints differ.
Implement hedging (speculative phase split exec) only for latency-priority tenants with a capped duplicate-token budget to control cost.
Default policy: balanced-mode; allow overrides per-tenant via Dedicated/Dedicated+ config in Console.
alternatives_considered: Strict priority lanes (hard isolation): rejected because it causes sustained throughput loss and underutilized kernels for mixed workloads.
Global static tuning knobs (single split configuration per model): too brittle across workload shifts and attention patterns.
Kernel-level speculative merging (remerge after kernel probe): promising but complex; deferred to follow-up if harmonizer shows promising results.
risks: Miscalibrated smoothing can harm throughput during long-tailed workloads — mitigated with conservative cap and rollout ramping
Kernel hint divergence: scheduler suggestions may not match hardware's optimal kernel selection under multi-tenancy — mitigate by soft hints and telemetry feedback loop
Increased observability overhead (additional metrics) could overload monitoring stack during experiments — create low-cardinality rollup metrics
notes: Next steps: tighten simulator workloads to include adversarial attention-sparsity patterns, implement feedback loop from kernel telemetry, schedule canary on dedicated-gpu pool with two tenants (one latency-priority, one throughput-priority).
